inventedEvidence.evidence: 'let me know what you found in the pump filter when you checked it earlier' (customer had not said so, but it was a request, not a stated fact)

confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'the heater is working fine; the issue is probably restricted airflow preventing moisture from escaping' despite the customer confirming a full 9kg load

rationale: The assistant correctly raised overload early and again in the final turn, but after the customer confirmed a full 9kg load it dropped that and sent them into the pump filter and condenser, asserting airflow restriction without evidence. It never asked about spin speed or suggested splitting loads until the very end, and the condenser-behind-the-pump-filter description appears invented. It also repeated the pump filter and condenser requests and wrongly implied the customer had already checked the filter. No part was recommended and there was no unsafe instruction, but the customer was sent on an unnecessary teardown before getting the likely answer.
